citation_verdicts.note: Stated as one of the principles organisations seeking value are 'likely to share', not a requirement; wording in the row is appropriately hedged.
The quote only points to Table 4, which is an image with a dead link; it supports that committees exist, not what they are. The row correctly flags Table 4 as unverifiable.
Text says 'often responsible'; the row's 'generally' for stewardship scope is fine, and 2.14 (C-54) says 'generally'.
Supports that issue resolution or facilitating it is steward work; this cuts against a blanket exclusion of issue handling from the steward role (see A-02).

Sentence is about understanding what, who is governed and who governs. The row (A-01) says the strategy defines an operating framework that settles who governs; that specific point rests on C-32, not on this quote.
Listed as one example of how policies 'may take different shapes'; illustrative only, as the row caveats.
Illustrative sample policy, as the row caveats.
Same sentence says escalation may go to Data Stewardship teams or higher to the DGC; the row's account is accurate.

The sentence says DG issue management relieves production-support burden. That implies DG does take on issue resolution, which sits in tension with, not clearly in support of, a role defined as not incident-resolution. It does not say governance and production support are separate roles; the row's inference is weak.
Appears as an example of concepts that can be standardised under the Data Quality knowledge area.

row_verdicts.note: Partial/wording is fair. Project states the draft-evaluate-approve split clearly; the only gap is that 'the appropriate human owner' is undefined in role terms.

Partial/structural-proposal is fair. The DMBOK2 counts identifying and resolving data issues as steward work (pp.151-152) while README and HANDOFF exclude 'operational incident resolution'; the row handles this correctly. The use of C-49 as support for the governance/production-support split is weak (see citation note).
Aligned/citation is fair: human approval of ownership assignment, no AI acting as Data Owner, and ownership gaps surfaced by the agent all match p.153 and p.169.
Partial/structural-proposal is fair. A named human governance owner exists in principle but is unnamed, with no bodies or escalation ladder defined.
Partial/wording is fair; policy, standards and procedures are not distinguished and standards adoption is not in the approval list.
Partial/structural-proposal is fair; governance reporting is only a bullet and the success criteria measure the AI system, not stewardship value.
Aligned/citation is fair for a scope-statement bullet; p.146 gives it only as a likely shared principle.

Aligned/citation is acceptable: human-only approval and DRAFT-NOT-APPROVED status match p.176. Mild inconsistency with A-01, where the unnamed approver is rated Partial; the p.176 point that approvers include core user-group representatives is not reflected in the project.
Partial/wording is fair; Chapter 3 has no thresholds or risk-acceptance text, so alignment rests on mapping to rules and standards.

missing_findings.note: Section 1.3.3 defines centralized, replicated and federated DG operating model types. It bears directly on the operating-model choice behind A-04 and the options, but is not cited.

Section 2.6 says the operating model defines the issue-management resolution pathways through governance and layers of accountability; supports the Partial finding on missing escalation path and is not cited (C-33 is cited from the same page for ownership only).

Steward definition (manage data assets on behalf of others, represent all stakeholders, a portion of time dedicated to DG activities) and p.153 Technical Data Stewards (including Data Quality Analysts) are not used; Technical Data Steward is listed in dmbok_terms but absent from the options.

Sample policy 'Business owners will designate Data Stewards from their business capability areas' bears on the owner/steward relationship (the project separates evaluating steward from approving owner) and is not cited.
Stewards 'should influence decisions' and are responsible for day-to-day adherence; relevant to the steward-evaluates, owner-approves split and not cited for A-01.

Standards enforcement and audit for compliance by the DGC and the point that data standards are usually drafted by data management professionals (a draft-then-approve pattern) are not cited for A-05; the row only uses the approval sentence.
